> Author: researcher (vfx-deep-research workflow) · claude-sonnet-5-5 · default · 2026-10-12

# P1 Elements: VALUE, COLOUR, TIMING

Scope: value, colour, timing for the future VFX-designer agent (Roblox, brick destruction first). Framework names used: gameplay, shape, value, colour, timing, composition. Timing words: windup, punch, crescendo, follow-through, dissipation.

Method notes (read first):
- WebSearch budget ran out mid-run (200/turn cap). Everything below was read by WebFetch or from the local Roblox mirror. Search snippets were used only to find URLs and are listed in section 6 as unread leads.
- Hard truth: **no named source read gives frame or ms numbers per VFX phase (windup/punch/dissipation).** The few real timing numbers are: hit stop example (Capcom), Spider-Verse step rates, first-quarter-of-lifetime rule (tier C, single source), tempo vs 60 BPM (tier C), flash safety (WCAG). Everything else in the timing rows is qualitative or marked inference.
- Evidence "inference" = my reasoning, not a source claim.

## 4. Conflicts between sources (newer first)

| topic | newer says | older says | resolution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Phase names | VFX Apprentice 2025 uses wind-up / climax / fall-off (S02) and a separate set windup / crescendo / follow-through / dissipation (S01) | Animation principles (anticipation, follow-through) in S27, S29 | Mapping for our agent: windup = wind-up/anticipation; punch = climax/pop; crescendo = build before punch (S02 defines crescendo as a build, not the peak); follow-through + dissipation = fall-off. Mapping is inference |
| Avoid pure white vs reserve pure white | S11 (2020): save 100% white for ultimates | S03 (2022, summarising 2017 guide): avoid 0/100 extremes | Not a real conflict: extremes are a scarce resource spent only on top-tier events. Our rule (inference): reserve for biggest punch |
| Dissipation style | S04 (2022): break up by subdividing instead of opacity fade | S14 (2023): blink-out can read clearer in an edge case | Both valid: breakup default; hard cut when gameplay clarity matters (stun trap) |
| Effects value vs UI | S14 (2023): norm = higher than characters, lower than UI | S14 same article: Sparkball breaks norm | Single source describes both; norm is a starting point, not a rule |
| Lingering | S03 (2022): don't linger | S04 (2022): Pixar poof clouds linger and dissipate slowly (film, not gameplay) | Different medium. Game effects share screen space with play; film effects own the shot |
| Frame rate "smooth is better" | S05/S06 (2023): lower rate gives stronger "pop" | S21 (2015): same finding for limited animation | Newer source confirms older; no change |
| Hit stop numbers | S13 (Capcom): 8/12/16F example | S23 (2024): comfort window exists, ms not read; S28 (D): up to 30F cap | Cannot reconcile without ms. Frame counts are game-specific |

## Verification log

Verifier: adversarial fact-check, 2026-10-12. Re-opened S02, S03, S05, S10, S11, S12, S13, S14, S19, S22, S28 (all fetched successfully). Not re-checked (time/scope): S04, S06, S08, S09, S15, S16, S17, S18, S20, S21, S23, S24, S25, S29 (unverified, rows left untagged).

Claims proved false and removed: none. Corrections applied (tags in rows):
- S14 25% rule: source allows dissipation to begin within the first quarter; the file implied the action must already be peak-then-erode. Single tier-C source still.
- S05 frame rates: "core look on 2s" and "1s..6s" are not stated for Hobie in S05; the 1s mention is a generic "2s, 3s, 1s, whatever". Core-on-2s is a foundational-technique statement, so keep as "on 2s is foundational" and rely on S06 for the range (S06 not re-checked).
- S12 blood: only a joke metaphor, not a stated policy.
- S28 formula: the Ultimate formula is a multi-step chain; file's shorthand was incomplete.

Confirmed with exact wording: S03 0/100 extremes and Keyser quote; S11 100% white for ultimates (2020-01-05; note S11 headline date in the table is correct, S09 date 2020-01-06 not re-checked); S10 1-10 rating; S14 UI quote and date; S02 60 BPM; S13 8F/12F/16F as hypothetical; S19 all flash numbers; S22 N=102, r=.57.

Notes on quotes: Section 3 quotes are under 15 words and match source. The Section 3 S11 quote omits the leading "We try to"; it is a verbatim fragment.

Tier notes: S12 (Riot dev blog) and S13 (Capcom official column) are first-party but are blog/column posts, not formal studies; "tier A" is defensible only as primary-source. S21, S07, S29 tier A were not re-opened. S19 and S20 are specs.

Gaps / missing tier-A sources: Riot 2017 style guide remains unread (all Riot value/colour claims are second-hand through tier-C VFX Apprentice and realtimevfx posts); no shipped-game frame/ms data for windup/punch/dissipation; the 25% and 60 BPM claims each rest on one tier-C blog; hit-stop comfort window (S23) is abstract-only; no peer-reviewed colour-emotion or bloom-perception study; the Riot "FX aren't supposed to be telling the story" quote stays unlocated.
